page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a verse passage at the head, followed by one long paragraph. Three notes stand in the left margin: "Cenfura." beside the line "pituita", "Anguil-læ curva lenter nutriát ?" beside "pigmento", and "Præc." beside "periculum".

main_text.p: Accipit hunc cœnum, quid enim fœcundius illo? Concipit accépto, nascuntur lubrica turba: Sic coeunt congri, sic lubrica membra refol-uunt.

Sed nobis perinde est, siue ex cœno, siue ex fœno, siue ex limo, siue ex fimo procreentur ur.[?] Quid in glo-ia œsophagi valeant, inquiramus. Certum[?] est anguillarum carnem medicos plerosque, omnes damnasse, tum in sanorum tum in ægrorum cibis, sed nulla probabili ratione, quod tamen pauci illorum dictum volo. Lenta enim illa & glu-tinosa[?] pituita,Cenfura. quam vescentibus pestem, imo largius crebriusq; sumtam, mortem afferre dicunt, elixatione, vel assatione sudando facile extillat, nullo relicto vel alieni saporis, vel lenti illius glu-tini Anguil-læ curva lenter nutriát ?pigmento. Parandi igitur ratio hic, quæ varia est, non ignoranda. In confesso est uberrimi alimenti esse anguillas ob carnem mollem & dulcem, adeoq; suauissimam[?] ad largissima edendum diuturno morbo confectos & extenuatos non al-liciat modo, verum etiam cito reficiat, vi-resq; restauret. Non eo inficias, uberius in cibis, crebriusq; sumtam, pernitiosam esse,Præc. vitæq; periculum afferre non assuetis. Itaque gentes in iis locis, ubi anguillarum abundantia est, (sic Homerus Phæacas appellat, ἀλωλιχωτάτας[?] quasi anguillis abundantissimos, & propterea in quotidiano sunt usu, paulatim iis edendis assuefacti, impune postea iis vescentur. page.notes: Running head and page number read as printed; "306" is a faint, slightly doubtful reading. "procreentur ur." has a doubled or split word at the line end; "Certum" is doubtful (the scan may read "Cerium"). "glu-tinosa" and "glu-tini": the word at the start of the second line of the paragraph is unclear, so the reading is doubtful. "suauissimam", "al-liciat" and "vi-resq;" are doubtful. The Greek phrase after "appellat" is only partly legible; it is given as best read, with [?]. The left-margin notes are "Cenfura.", "Anguil-læ curva lenter nutriát ?" and "Præc.". The catchword "memi-" is printed at the bottom right. The verse at the head is set as one stanza.
